title: Policy override saga and controlplane recovery cheatsheet
content:
Purpose
This note captures a compact operational runbook embedded inside architecture context for policy overrides, control plane divergence, and multi-region recovery. It is intended for on-call platform engineers and SREs during routing anomalies where the control plane state is inconsistent with data plane behavior or when steering policies unexpectedly flip traffic across regions.

Scope and intent
- Describe observable symptoms that indicate policy drift or control plane corruption.
- Provide immediate mitigation steps to preserve SLOs and limit blast radius.
- Detail safe recovery and verification steps for a staged return to normal policy state.
- Provide quick automation commands and manual fallbacks when automation is compromised.

Background context (short)
Redwood routing decisions are made by the control plane, which publishes policy bundles to edge routers and regional proxies. A policy bundle includes: routing weights, circuit breaker thresholds, failover maps, and model variant preference lists. Staleness or inconsistent application of bundles can result from partial rollout, migration logic bugs, or control plane DB corruption. Because traffic steering decisions are latency-sensitive, the data plane caches policies with TTLs and uses local heuristics when updates are delayed.

Alert triggers and initial triage (fast check list)
1) Alerts that typically indicate policy/control plane issues:
   - Sudden spike in 5xxs localized to one region while upstream capacity looks healthy (Alert: ERR-RATE-REGION-THRESH).
   - Rapid increase in cross-region egress traffic and inter-region latency (Alert: XREG-EGRESS-ANOMALY).
   - Discrepancy between control plane reported routing weights and data plane telemetry (Alert: POLICY-DIFF-DET).
   - SLO breach for p95 latency with no corresponding infra CPU/GPU saturation (Alert: LAT-SLO-MISSING-CAUSE).
2) Quick triage steps (first 5 minutes):
   - Check controller health: kubectl get pods -n controlplane; look for CrashLoopBackOff or OOMKill.
   - Fetch last policy bundle publish event: curl -s https://controlplane.internal/api/bundles/latest or check GitHub PR deployment logs.
   - Compare last bundle ID on control plane vs representative regional proxy: run proxyctl get-bundle --region eu-west-1 --bundle-id.
   - Check audit trail for manual policy override actions: ELK search policy.override by user.
   - Confirm rollout window and scheduled jobs: Jenkins/ArgoCD windows.

Immediate mitigation (first 10-30 minutes)
Goal: stop bad policy propagation and stabilize traffic. Prioritize preserving p99 latency and error rate.
Option A: Pause releases and freeze bundle propagation
   - Trigger gate: create a temporary maintenance flag in control plane: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/maintenance -d '{skip_publish: true, reason: policy-rollback}'
   - If automation cannot accept API calls, scale down publisher controller: kubectl scale deployment controlplane-publisher --replicas=0 -n controlplane (only if safe)
   - Notify regions to extend policy TTLs to avoid abrupt local policy expirations.
Option B: Force fallback to last known-good policy bundle
   - Identify last-known-good bundle ID from S3 keys or bundle history.
   - Use controlplane rollback API: POST /api/bundles/rollback body: {bundle_id: "bkg-2026-02-26-1812"}.
   - Verify regional proxies have applied the BKG bundle: proxyctl tail-logs --grep apply-bundle --region ap-south-1

Traffic steering and circuit breaker adjustments
   - If cross-region egress spike is occurring, temporarily raise circuit breaker thresholds to avoid cascading retries across regions: adjust config map cb-config to 2x threshold and apply.
   - If a region is failing due to bad routing weight, pin traffic to local region with runbook command: routingctl set-weight --route inference-api --region us-west-2 --weight 100 --force. Only for <30 minutes, and require page to on-call lead.

Escalation matrix and communication
- Pager to platform-oncall and eng-serving-runtime if any of the following holds: region-wide 5xx > 3x baseline for 5 minutes, rollback fails, or control plane DB shows corruption.
- Slack channel: #plat-incident, thread name: POLICY-OVERRIDE-<region>-<time>. Include bundle IDs, cluster IDs, recent deploys.
- Escalate to product security if manual override user is external service account or unknown.

Safe rollback and state reconciliation (30-90 minutes)
1) Once traffic stabilized on BKG bundle, collect diagnostics:
   - controlplane logs: journalctl -u controlplane | grep bundle
   - DB snapshot checksums: run db-checksum.sh --since 48h
   - Compare policy diff: policy-diff-tool --left bkg-id --right last-id > /tmp/policy-diff.txt
2) If diff is small and intentional, prepare a controlled incremental rollout with canary
   - Create canary environment with 1% traffic using routingctl canary create --bundle new-bundle --pct 1
   - Observe for 30m: errors, latency, inter-region egress, and cache churn.
3) If control plane DB shows inconsistencies, do not attempt automated repair. Capture DB snapshot and escalate to platform database team.

Manual fallbacks (when tooling is down)
- If control plane APIs are unreachable but regional proxies still accept manual commands, perform region-local overrides: ssh to proxy machines, update /etc/proxy/policies/bundles and send SIGHUP to proxy process.
- As last resort, update edge load balancer rules to route around problematic region: terraform apply with LB override module. Ensure emergency change is tracked and short-lived.

Verification checklist before restore to normal
- All regions report bundle_id = target-bundle-id for >= 5 minutes.
- p95 and error rates back within 1.2x baseline for 30 minutes.
- No unexplained spike in inter-region traffic.
- Control plane publisher and DB show no restarts for 1 hour.
- Postmortem owner assigned and timeline captured.

Post-incident: follow-up and durable fixes
Short-term remediation candidates:
- Add stricter preflight validation to policy bundles in CI (reject induces of negative weight sums, contradictory failover maps).
- Improve bundle publish observability: surface bundle diffs in the console and generate auto-alerts when data plane reports mismatch.
- Harden RBAC: limit manual override permission to specific service accounts with MFA.
Longer-term design items:
- Implement transactional bundle apply across regions or two-phase commit semantics for critical keys.
- Add cross-region canary control: require telemetry agreement across two control points before global rollout.

Runbook snippets and common commands
- Check last published bundle: curl -s https://controlplane.internal/api/bundles/latest | jq .id
- Force rollback: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/bundles/rollback -d '{"bundle_id":"bkg-2026-02-26-1812"}'
- Verify proxy bundle: proxyctl get-bundle --proxy-id proxy-eu-1 --output json | jq .bundle_id
- Scale down publisher: kubectl scale deployment controlplane-publisher --replicas=0 -n controlplane

Known unknowns and open questions
- TTL semantics: how long should proxies honor a bundle when publisher is offline before falling into local heuristics? Need a clear SLA.
- Two-phase commit impact on latency: trade-offs between atomicity and publish speed for high-frequency policy updates.
- Can we use the model of leader-election for bundle apply to minimize partial application? Proof-of-concept needed.

Appendix: quick timeline template for incident page
- T0: Alert fired and severity assigned
- T0+5m: publisher health check and last bundle inspection
- T0+15m: mitigation applied (pause publish or rollback)
- T0+45m: metrics stabilized or escalation to DB team
- T0+2h: controlled canary and observation window
- T0+4h: rollback or acceptance and begin restore to normal

RCA prompts for postmortem
- What sequence of events led to policy divergence between control and data plane?
- Were there CI checks that could have caught the bad bundle?
- Did human overrides follow the documented escalation path?
- How effective were circuit breakers in preventing cascading failures?

Contact and ownership
- Primary runbook owner: Priya Shah (platform engineering)
- Backup: Liam Rodriguez
- Database escalation: Zoe Kim

Notes to reviewers
This doc is intentionally concise to be used in a paging context. It does not replace full design docs. After next incident, convert learnings into the policy lifecycle design page and add concrete automation tests to CI.

End of document
